reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the role of O/N interstitials in causing α-Ti precipitation and softening in a Ti-V-Nb-Ta RHEA at 700°C. However, the hypothesis extends this mechanism to Ti- and Ni-containing HEAs as primary constituents without any cited evidence for such alloys; the transferability of the mechanism across different alloy systems is a key unsupported premise.
premises: Trace oxygen and nitrogen interstitials promote phase segregation during high-temperature aging in refractory HEAs.
This segregation (e.g., α-Ti precipitates) depletes solid-solution strengthening elements and causes softening.
Reducing interstitial impurities will prevent such precipitate formation and preserve the single-phase solid solution.
Preserving the single-phase solid solution will retain or improve high-temperature strength.
These mechanisms, observed in Ti-V-Nb-Ta, apply to Ti- and Ni-containing HEAs as primary constituents.
